questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signals whenever you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid fixating on one spot for too long.

questions.question: You should turn on your headlights:

options.text: One half hour after sunset.
One half hour after sunrise.
When parked at a school.
When stopped at a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Use headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when it is raining or snowing, or when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching them. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angrily:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When another driver is angry, get away from them. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you safely can to stay out of danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is showing red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is showing green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:

options.text: Deaf.
Part of a traffic study.
Blind.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind person. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Don't speed on wet roads.
Keep tires filled to the right air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Enter it slowly and let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, how can you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a sober friend.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a sober friend.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who is not drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your body. Your body takes about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Drive slower.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where there are pedestrians, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road intersects with a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road intersects with a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a median or rail between them.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are making a turn.
Your emergency brake is on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must always work properly when you drive.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
You must give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection. You can continue driving, but drive at a speed where you can stop if the light changes.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, not what the flagger says.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.explanation: Always obey flaggers and slow down in construction zones. Not following their directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A red light means you must come to a complete stop. Running a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign forbidding it.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the chance of death in a crash. Above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is very unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make unsafe passing moves.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to clear a path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to clear a path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, you must slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers when you are turning.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than normal.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: Slippery roads are especially dangerous in turns and curves. Slow down more for turns when roads are wet or icy than you would on dry roads.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey over the others?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs and signals. Other people authorized to direct traffic include fire police, highway work zone flaggers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until that vehicle safely passes before you go.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far or as clearly in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far or as clearly in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, your vision is limited. Always use proper headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before moving into it.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes pulling toward or away from a curb, turning, and changing lanes.

questions.question: Orange signs are:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers that construction or maintenance work is happening on the road. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters and symbols.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell any passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver's license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Keep driving carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop completely before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Only go when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off before you go.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them feel normal again?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.explanation: Only time will allow a person's body to get over the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways. Only go if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly go under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways. Only go if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from either direction before crossing. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The possible speeds you could drive in that area
The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest and slowest legal speeds for that road. These limits are for good conditions. You must drive slower when weather or traffic is bad.

questions.question: You had a bad day at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to calm down.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
Stop and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?

options.text: Yes, as long as a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle fits without hitting the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Wait until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up before you cross. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Heavy traffic ahead.
Do not enter.
Railroad crossing.
Yield.

questions.explanation: This sign means it is not safe to enter the road or driveway from where you are. If you see this sign, turn around and find another way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What is true about traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should ensure your physical condition is good. What should you do?

options.text: Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.
Know how medicine affects your driving ability.
Drive only when you are within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Stay physically fit, know how medicine affects you, and only drive when you can do so safely.

questions.question: The MVC may stop your road test before it starts if:

options.text: Your vehicle is unsafe.
Equipment in your vehicle blocks access to the brake pedal.
Your vehicle is missing seat belts.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: The examiner may stop your road test if your vehicle is unsafe, blocks access to the brake pedal, or is missing seat belts.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Frequent rest stops.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.
Short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: "Highway hypnosis" happens when you stare straight ahead for a long time and stop looking around. This makes you zone out and miss traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other motorists.
Street lights.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs or other roadside objects.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator and gently apply the brakes. Pull off the road into a safe area.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Pull over to the right side of the road. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to illuminate the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility. Drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams to better see the road and objects ahead.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Stay out of traffic lanes. Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.
